_about: A330-200, from Airbus AC A330 (Dec 01/25) 2-2-0 General Aircraft Dimensions, A330-200 sheets 2 (post mod 48979; side, front: page index 62) and 3 (plan: page index 63). Pixels of layers.py --mode strokes-in-fill rasters, line centres: 80.775 px a meter (the sheet's own scale, from the printed 58.82 m between its extension lines): the side at scale 16 stretched lengthwise by 1.00971 (--xscale: the sheet draws the aircraft 1% short of that length, its height at that scale) and turned level (--rotate -0.556), the plan at 15.028 stretched by 1.0030 (its across scale from its printed figures), the front at 15.893. The A330-300's points moved onto these sheets and snapped (a332/*.anchors.json says how); the fin, taller than the -300's, is placed here. Scaled by the printed 58.82 m overall length from the nose to the tail cone. The windows behind the wing's lines and one behind a dimension line are placed at the drawing's pitch; door 3 is drawn only above the wing: its height is the A330-300's. After build.py, the tail cone's last 2 m (crown from 56.8 m, belly from 58.1 m) are the A330-300's shape file's, moved by the 4.85 m shorter fuselage: the tailplane is traced into this sheet's (docs/SHAPES.md); and the winglet is the A330-300's, moved onto this wing's tip (this sheet's own winglet trace crosses itself), the wing's last height the A330-300's tip's; then smooth.py.

sources.title: Airbus, A330 Aircraft Characteristics: Airport and Maintenance Planning (Dec 01/25), 2-2-0 General Aircraft Dimensions, A330-200 sheets 2 (post mod 48979) and 3
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/a332/), starting from the A330-300's points moved by the shorter fuselage; the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The sheet draws the aircraft 1% shorter than the printed 58.82 m between its own extension lines, at their scale across: the side and plan are stretched lengthwise to them, so the length and the printed 5.64 m height share one scale (scaled by the length alone, the height read 1.1% tall). The side view is turned level from the sheet's ground attitude (0.56°). Engine out from the centerline: half the printed 18.74 m between the engines. The cockpit panes are the A330-300's (the same nose).
